landing.title: Join landing backgrounds help
landing.summary: This screen controls the responsive visual background behind sign-in and signup on friending.com. A protected image-free fallback always exists, while optional global, country and city campaigns can provide images or video.

steps.1: Start with the protected fallback and confirm that login remains readable without campaign media.
steps.2: For a campaign, define the geographic scope and priority before uploading responsive media and appearance settings.
steps.3: Preview desktop, tablet and mobile inheritance, then activate only the reviewed rule.

fallback.title: Protected media-free fallback
fallback.purpose: The fallback guarantees that Join can render a usable login surface even when no campaign matches or media cannot load.

actions.1: Edit its gradient and login contrast card without attaching image or video media.
actions.2: Use it as the visual safety net for every campaign.

fallback.guidance: The fallback cannot be deleted. Keep it readable and brand-appropriate because it is the final resolution for every failed or unmatched rule.

targeting.title: Global, country and city targeting
targeting.purpose: Rules can apply everywhere, to one ISO country, or near a city center within a bounded radius.

actions.1: Select the smallest intended scope and enter canonical country or city coordinates when required.
actions.2: Review how the rule competes with other matching campaigns.

targeting.guidance: Geographic targeting is presentation selection, not a member-profile location change. Use verified codes and coordinates rather than approximate guesses.

responsiveMedia.title: Responsive image or video
responsiveMedia.purpose: Desktop media is required for a media rule and becomes the fallback for tablet or mobile variants that are left empty.

actions.1: Choose image or video and supply the required desktop asset.
actions.2: Add tablet or mobile variants only when they materially improve the crop or performance.

responsiveMedia.guidance: Test every supplied variant and the inherited fallback. Large or poorly cropped media can obscure authentication even when the desktop preview looks correct.

videoPosters.title: Video poster images
videoPosters.purpose: Optional posters provide a stable visual while video loads or when autoplay is delayed, with desktop cascading to missing smaller variants.

actions.1: Upload a poster that matches the first usable video frame.
actions.2: Add device-specific posters only when needed.

videoPosters.guidance: A poster does not replace the video URL validation. Check that the page remains readable when only the poster is visible.

gradient.title: Landing gradient overlay
gradient.purpose: The continuous gradient preserves upper media visibility while building controlled contrast near the footer and authentication content.

actions.1: Choose the desktop color and intensity.
actions.2: Enable tablet or mobile overrides only after previewing inheritance.

gradient.guidance: The overlay works with or without media. Avoid transparent settings that make legal or login content unreadable over bright assets.

loginCard.title: Login contrast card
loginCard.purpose: A rounded blurred card behind authentication controls keeps fields, buttons and legal links readable across backgrounds.

actions.1: Tune desktop color, opacity, blur and shape within the supported bounds.
actions.2: Preview inherited and overridden tablet or mobile cards.

loginCard.guidance: Readability and focus visibility are more important than matching a single campaign image. Test the image-free fallback too.

priorityLifecycle.title: Priority, activation and deletion
priorityLifecycle.purpose: Priority resolves overlapping matches, while active state controls eligibility and deletion removes a rule from future selection.

actions.1: Use higher priority only when a campaign must win over another matching rule.
actions.2: Deactivate for a reversible pause; delete only after confirming the exact rule.

priorityLifecycle.guidance: Equal-priority city rules choose the nearest center. Deleting a rule retains uploaded media files, so deletion is not a media cleanup tool.

appLanding.title: App landing screen help
appLanding.summary: This page controls the iOS screen shown before sign-in: background, Friending title treatment and bilingual description. A global rule supplies defaults and country or city overrides may inherit any blank field.

steps.1: Establish and review the global rule because every override and built-in fallback resolves through it.
steps.2: For an override, fill only the fields that genuinely differ and verify its geographic priority.
steps.3: Use the resolved preview to confirm the final background, title and description before activation.

rules.title: Landing rule inventory
rules.purpose: Cards list the global source and every geographic override with active state, priority and resolved presentation preview.

actions.1: Create the required global rule first, then add or edit overrides.
actions.2: Review which values each override supplies and which it inherits.

rules.guidance: The protected global rule cannot be deleted like an ordinary override. Without it, the app uses only its built-in screen.

targeting.title: Geographic targeting and priority
targeting.purpose: A rule can be global, country-wide or centered on a city radius, with priority resolving overlapping matches.

actions.1: Choose a canonical ISO country and bounded city radius where applicable.
actions.2: Set priority relative to other rules that can match the same user context.

targeting.guidance: Targeting chooses presentation and is not written to the member profile. Equal-priority cities use the nearest center.

background.title: Background image or video
background.purpose: The rule may supply an approved image or CDN video with an optional poster, or leave the background blank to inherit.

actions.1: Select the media type and upload or enter the trusted asset.
actions.2: Leave an override blank when the global background should continue to apply.

background.guidance: Blank means inherit, not black. Test video loading and poster behavior on a supported app build before activation.

title.title: Text or image title
title.purpose: The Friending title can be bilingual text or a transparent PNG treatment, with blank override text inheriting the global or built-in title.

actions.1: Choose text and complete both locales, or upload the required transparent title image.
actions.2: Switch back to text before removing an image title.

title.guidance: A title-image rule without its asset is invalid. Keep transparent artwork readable over every resolved background.

description.title: Bilingual description
description.purpose: The short English and Hungarian copy explains the pre-sign-in value proposition under the title.

actions.1: Write concise, consistent copy in both languages.
actions.2: Leave override copy blank only when inheritance is intentional.

description.guidance: The preview resolves blank values, so review the final sentence rather than assuming an empty editor means no description.

previewInheritance.title: Resolved preview and lifecycle
previewInheritance.purpose: The preview calculates the actual rule, then global rule, then built-in fallback chain and shows what the app should receive.

actions.1: Verify every resolved visual and localized string before saving or activating.
actions.2: Deactivate for a reversible pause or delete only the intended non-global rule.

previewInheritance.guidance: A preview is meaningful only for the loaded revision. Refresh after conflicts, and remember that deleting a rule retains its stored media files.

signupOptions.title: Signup options help
signupOptions.summary: This workspace defines the questions and selectable answers used while a person creates a Friending profile. It distinguishes protected identity axes from optional questions and controls bilingual labels, icons and who is eligible to see each choice.

steps.1: Find the question and first decide whether it is a protected system axis or an editable optional group.
steps.2: Review question presentation, answer choices and audience rules together before changing any one of them.
steps.3: Save or archive the narrowest item and verify that existing member answers remain understandable.

workspace.title: Compact signup workspace
workspace.purpose: Search and expandable question cards keep the complete signup catalog manageable without loading every answer editor at once.

actions.1: Search by key or bilingual label and expand only the question you need.
actions.2: Use the overview warnings to distinguish protected system behavior from editable presentation.

workspace.guidance: Signup choices can influence discovery and audiences. Do not treat the catalog as cosmetic copy only.

questions.title: Question presentation and policy
questions.purpose: Each question has stable identity, bilingual name, optional managed icon, required state, order and—where permitted—an audience.

actions.1: Edit English and Hungarian titles and upload a trusted icon.
actions.2: For non-system groups, review order, required state and availability rules.

questions.guidance: Protected system questions keep their key and policy because Core and clients depend on them. Matching orientation is separate from optional profile-orientation disclosure.

answers.title: Selectable answers
answers.purpose: Answer rows provide the choices members can select under a question; system choices normally permit display-name edits while custom extensible groups permit new stable options.

actions.1: Rename permitted bilingual labels without changing the stable meaning.
actions.2: Add a custom option only to a group designed for extension.

answers.guidance: A permanent key carries stored member meaning. Never reuse an old key for a different identity, gender or orientation concept.

audiences.title: Question and answer audiences
audiences.purpose: Audience rules can limit optional questions or custom answers by canonical gender and dynamic user groups, with selected dimensions intersecting.

actions.1: Leave all selectors empty for global availability where the group permits it.
actions.2: Choose only the genders and groups that product policy intends to receive the question or answer.

audiences.guidance: When multiple dimensions are set, every dimension must match. An overly narrow rule can make a choice disappear for legitimate members.

archiveBehavior.title: Archive and preserved answers
archiveBehavior.purpose: Archiving removes an optional choice from new selection while keeping existing stored answers readable and recoverable.

actions.1: Read the confirmation and archive only the obsolete option.
actions.2: Edit or restore a retired option when its original meaning returns.

archiveBehavior.guidance: Archive is not destructive cleanup. Existing member data remains by design, and protected system answers cannot be removed.

signupPhotos.title: Signup photos help
signupPhotos.summary: This page configures the photo part of registration: how many profile pictures are required or allowed, the moderation notice, the dedicated first-avatar screen and visual tip cards that teach members to choose a useful photo.

steps.1: Review minimum and maximum upload rules together so registration remains completable.
steps.2: Keep avatar and moderation copy complete in English and Hungarian.
steps.3: Preview and order every tip card, then save one revision and confirm the refreshed document.

photoGrid.title: Profile picture count rules
photoGrid.purpose: Minimum photos decides when Continue unlocks; maximum photos caps the signup grid and can never exceed six.

actions.1: Set a supported minimum and maximum that fit the intended signup experience.
actions.2: Review automatic coupling when raising the minimum above the previous maximum.

photoGrid.guidance: Higher requirements can block completion for members with limited suitable media. Validate the app flow before increasing them.

moderationNotice.title: Photo moderation notice
moderationNotice.purpose: The optional notice explains that uploaded photos may be reviewed and links to the relevant policy page.

actions.1: Enable the row only with complete bilingual copy and an HTTPS policy link.
actions.2: Disable it to hide the entire notice when policy explicitly allows that.

moderationNotice.guidance: The link may use any HTTPS policy host, so verify ownership and content manually. Disabling copy here does not disable backend moderation.

avatarScreen.title: Dedicated first-avatar screen
avatarScreen.purpose: This controls the title, subtitle and tips-box heading shown around the member's first profile-photo tile.

actions.1: Write clear, consistent English and Hungarian guidance.
actions.2: Check that the copy explains the task without promising automatic approval.

avatarScreen.guidance: This is often a new member's first media decision. Keep wording practical and avoid technical moderation terminology.

tipCards.title: Photo tip cards
tipCards.purpose: Up to twelve cards combine a default image, optional men's variant, bilingual caption, stable key and display order.

actions.1: Add, edit, reorder or remove a card in the local draft.
actions.2: Upload a required default picture and use a men's variant only when the visual advice needs it.

tipCards.guidance: The default image is shown to everyone unless the specific variant applies. Stable keys must be unique, and every used card needs both language captions.

userGroups.title: User groups help
userGroups.summary: User groups are server-evaluated member segments used to show restricted profile questions. Membership is calculated from gender and matching-orientation rules; one member can belong to several groups at the same time.

steps.1: Understand the existing system groups and any audience that references them before editing rules.
steps.2: Build rules from canonical gender and matching orientation only, then review the resulting intent.
steps.3: Save, reorder or archive with awareness that field audiences may immediately gain or lose matches.

groupList.title: Cast group inventory
groupList.purpose: The list shows system and custom groups in display order with bilingual labels, active state, rules and member-count context.

actions.1: Review or reorder groups and open one for editing.
actions.2: Create a custom group when a new audience cannot be represented safely by existing groups.

groupList.guidance: The six system groups reproduce proven casts and cannot be archived. A group is a rule, not a manually maintained member list.

membershipRules.title: Gender and matching-orientation rules
membershipRules.purpose: A member belongs when any rule matches both their canonical gender and required matching orientation.

actions.1: Add one or more precise rule cards and review their OR relationship.
actions.2: Update labels and order independently from matching logic.

membershipRules.guidance: Optional profile-orientation disclosure must never enter these rules. Changing rules can alter visibility for many members immediately.

legacyProjection.title: Legacy segment compatibility
legacyProjection.purpose: An optional legacy segment lets older surfaces project the first matching compatible group into the classic cast model.

actions.1: Retain the fixed mapping on system groups.
actions.2: Set a custom compatibility projection only when an older client contract explicitly needs it.

legacyProjection.guidance: Display order can decide which compatible group wins the legacy projection. Review order and segment together.

archiveBehavior.title: Activation and archive impact
archiveBehavior.purpose: Deactivation or archive stops the group matching members and removes it from future audience selection without rewriting every referring field.

actions.1: Read the impact confirmation before archiving a custom group.
actions.2: Reactivate or correct the original group when its meaning should return.

archiveBehavior.guidance: Existing field audiences that reference an archived group simply stop matching through it. Confirm all known consumers before the change.

profileFields.title: Profile fields help
profileFields.summary: Profile fields are the bilingual questions members answer after signup. This page controls where questions appear, which members receive them, their selectable answers and how retired content remains readable on existing profiles.

steps.1: Review profile-section layout and audience gates before editing a question or answer.
steps.2: Use stable keys and complete both languages, then preview selection rules and icon behavior.
steps.3: Save or archive one bounded catalog item and check the member-impact warning.

sectionLayout.title: Profile section layout
sectionLayout.purpose: The layout places every eligible question once across Main data, More about you and Let's go deeper, with bilingual section copy and optional Layer 2 visibility gates.

actions.1: Drag or move fields between sections and order them for member readability.
actions.2: Set section titles, subtitles, hidden state and reviewed Layer 2 gates.

sectionLayout.guidance: Layout changes presentation, while field audience controls eligibility. A Layer 2 gate can further hide a section and must reflect the reciprocal disclosure policy.

catalogSearch.title: Question catalog and search
catalogSearch.purpose: Search locates active and archived questions by stable key or localized label, and expandable cards keep large answer lists manageable.

actions.1: Find and expand the intended field.
actions.2: Create a custom field only when an existing one cannot carry the new meaning.

catalogSearch.guidance: System-owned fields retain protected semantics. Do not create a duplicate custom question to bypass a system policy.

fieldEditor.title: Question editor
fieldEditor.purpose: A field defines its permanent key, bilingual labels, optional managed icon, selection mode, required counts, order, active state and audience.

actions.1: Complete both locales and choose single or bounded multiple selection.
actions.2: Upload only a trusted PNG or sanitized SVG and set a deliberate order.

fieldEditor.guidance: A key cannot be renamed after creation because clients and stored answers depend on it. Changing selection limits can affect future edits to existing profiles.

answerOptions.title: Selectable answer options
answerOptions.purpose: Options provide the bilingual values a member can select under one field, each with a permanent key, order and active state.

actions.1: Add, rename, reorder or archive an option within its owning field.
actions.2: Keep the option's meaning stable when editing display copy.

answerOptions.guidance: Archived answers remain readable for members who already selected them. Never recycle a key for a new meaning.

audience.title: Field audience
audience.purpose: Audience can be global or restricted by canonical gender, built-in casts and dynamic groups; configured dimensions must all match.

actions.1: Leave global when every eligible member should receive the question.
actions.2: Select the smallest reviewed audience and inspect its group definitions.

audience.guidance: Audience changes can hide a question from existing members while preserving their answer. Treat widening as a disclosure-policy change, not a simple catalog edit.

archiveBehavior.title: Archive and member-answer preservation
archiveBehavior.purpose: Archiving a field or option stops new selection but preserves stored answers so profiles and support history do not lose meaning.

actions.1: Review the affected-entry warning before confirming archive.
actions.2: Use archive instead of deleting or repurposing stable catalog records.

archiveBehavior.guidance: Preserved answers can remain visible or removable according to client policy. Archive is intentionally not a bulk data deletion.

profilePresentation.title: Profile presentation help
profilePresentation.summary: This page chooses which public-safe facts appear directly below the photo gallery as highlighted chips and which appear later as More About Me rows. It controls layout and labels, not the member's underlying answers.

steps.1: Review every available source and identify which are public-safe, dedicated or intentionally unavailable.
steps.2: Build the two ordered destinations in the local draft and edit built-in labels or managed icons only when needed.
steps.3: Check the semantic preview, then save the complete revision once.

draftToolbar.title: Draft and save toolbar
draftToolbar.purpose: All drag, move and source edits stay local until the complete presentation document is saved against the current revision.

actions.1: Review the dirty-state indicator and discard to return to the last Core version.
actions.2: Save the full ordered draft after previewing both destinations.

draftToolbar.guidance: Navigation with an unsaved draft can lose work. A revision conflict must adopt and re-review the server copy rather than merge blindly.

highlights.title: Highlighted chips
highlights.purpose: These compact public facts appear immediately below the profile hero gallery and therefore shape the first profile impression.

actions.1: Move allowed sources into the highlight list and order them by importance.
actions.2: Remove a source back to Unused without deleting its underlying member data.

highlights.guidance: Keep the row concise. A fact being public-safe does not mean it belongs in the most prominent position.

moreAbout.title: More About Me rows
moreAbout.purpose: These icon, label and one-line value rows appear lower in Profile Details for useful context that does not need hero prominence.

actions.1: Assign and order allowed sources in the longer-form section.
actions.2: Edit built-in bilingual label and trusted icon when the source supports it.

moreAbout.guidance: Changing presentation labels affects every member using the built-in source. Keep the label faithful to the stored value.

unusedSources.title: Unused and dedicated sources
unusedSources.purpose: The inventory explains which sources are available for placement, currently unused, dedicated to another surface or private and therefore locked.

actions.1: Move an eligible source to one destination.
actions.2: Read the lock reason for a dedicated or private source instead of trying to expose it.

unusedSources.guidance: A source can appear only once. Private or dedicated values remain visible in the inventory for transparency, not as an invitation to bypass their boundary.

preview.title: Semantic profile preview
preview.purpose: The preview shows the two destinations with male, female or neutral accent semantics owned by clients rather than storing client colors in Core.

actions.1: Switch accent roles and inspect order, labels and icon balance.
actions.2: Use the preview to catch an empty or overloaded destination.

preview.guidance: The preview demonstrates structure, not every device size or real member value. Validate supported clients for a major layout change.

profileTags.title: Profile tag catalogs help
profileTags.summary: These three catalogs—What I'm Into, My Story and Interests—supply grouped chips members can select for their profile. Each catalog has its own bilingual introduction, selection limits, audiences, ordering and member-impact safeguards.

steps.1: Choose the correct catalog tab and review unsaved-state, revision and member-selection warnings.
steps.2: Edit catalog rules, groups or items while preserving permanent keys and existing selection meaning.
steps.3: Run an audience preview, then save the complete catalog and verify reconciliation counts.

catalogTabs.title: Separate catalog tabs
catalogTabs.purpose: Tabs isolate the three profile experiences and mark which local draft contains unsaved changes.

actions.1: Select What I'm Into, My Story or Interests before editing.
actions.2: Resolve or discard the current draft before switching when prompted.

catalogTabs.guidance: The catalogs have separate revisions and legacy fields. A change intended for one must not be copied mechanically to the others.

catalogRules.title: Catalog title and selection rules
catalogRules.purpose: The catalog-level panel controls bilingual title, subtitle, minimum and maximum selections and active presentation settings.

actions.1: Edit both locales and keep minimum no higher than maximum.
actions.2: Reset to the loaded revision or save the complete draft.

catalogRules.guidance: Lowering a maximum does not erase members' existing excess selections; they retain them until a later profile edit.

groupsItems.title: Groups and tag items
groupsItems.purpose: Groups organize tag chips, while each item belongs to exactly one group and carries a permanent key, bilingual label, icon or emoji, order and active state.

actions.1: Add, edit, drag or use arrows to order groups and items.
actions.2: Move an item to one target group or archive it without duplicating its identity.

groupsItems.guidance: Member selection counts reveal impact. Moving or archiving a selected item preserves it as retired and removable rather than silently rewriting profiles.

audience.title: Group and item audience
audience.purpose: Rows can be global or restricted by canonical gender and server-derived segment, with all configured dimensions required to match.

actions.1: Leave both lists empty for global availability.
actions.2: Apply only reviewed restrictions and compare group-level and item-level intent.

audience.guidance: Audience widening can disclose a profile choice to a new group. Existing selections are grandfathered through narrowing so members can still remove them.

preview.title: Synthetic audience preview
preview.purpose: The preview asks Core for the active localized catalog visible to a chosen synthetic gender and segment context without identifying or persisting a real member.

actions.1: Choose a language, gender and segment to inspect the resolved catalog.
actions.2: Repeat for each affected audience before saving.

preview.guidance: A preview proves only the selected synthetic context. It does not replace checking every audience combination changed by the draft.

icebreakers.title: Icebreaker cards help
icebreakers.summary: Icebreakers are optional profile prompts that help members start conversations or express themselves. This page controls bilingual question copy, Friends/Sex/Love placement, who may answer and whether a prompt remains available.

steps.1: Search for an existing prompt before creating a new one with overlapping meaning.
steps.2: Set card placement and member audience independently and complete both languages.
steps.3: Save or archive while preserving existing profile answers.

search.title: Prompt search and inventory
search.purpose: Search filters the complete prompt catalog while the count and cards show active, archived, grouped and targeted prompts.

actions.1: Find by stable key or localized question.
actions.2: Open a prompt for editing or start a new one.

search.guidance: Similar questions fragment member answers. Prefer improving an existing prompt when its stable meaning is the same.

promptEditor.title: Bilingual prompt editor
promptEditor.purpose: The editor defines a permanent key, English and Hungarian question, order and active state while preserving any future locales returned by Core.

actions.1: Write concise questions in both required languages.
actions.2: Set order and active state without renaming the stable key.

promptEditor.guidance: A key cannot be renamed later. The question should invite an answer without requesting sensitive or unsafe disclosure.

placementAudience.title: Friends, Sex, Love placement and audience
placementAudience.purpose: Placement selects where the card appears; audience independently controls which eligible genders and dynamic groups can answer it.

actions.1: Choose one or more appropriate thematic groups.
actions.2: Leave audience global or select a reviewed restricted audience.

placementAudience.guidance: Placement does not imply eligibility. When multiple audience dimensions are set they all must match, so test the intended member groups.

archiveBehavior.title: Archive and existing answers
archiveBehavior.purpose: Archiving removes the prompt from new answer selection while profiles that already answered it keep readable content.

actions.1: Confirm the exact question before archiving.
actions.2: Restore or edit the original prompt if its stable meaning becomes active again.

archiveBehavior.guidance: Archive is not deletion of member-generated answers. Removing historical content requires a separate member or moderation flow.

layer2Intents.title: Layer 2 intents help
layer2Intents.summary: Layer 2 is the catalog behind “What brings you to Friending”. Members choose a small number of intents, and an answer is disclosed only to another member who selected an intent in the same reciprocal set.

steps.1: Read catalog readiness and current selection limit before editing any item.
steps.2: Preserve the item's permanent identity, Layer 1 placement and reciprocal set while completing label and glossary in both languages.
steps.3: Save against both revisions, then archive and replace rather than retargeting a live disclosure set.

readiness.title: Catalog readiness
readiness.purpose: Readiness summarizes whether every active item has complete bilingual member copy and a structurally valid place in the bounded catalog.

actions.1: Review incomplete or withheld items before changing selection policy.
actions.2: Complete both labels and glossaries so Core can serve an item.

readiness.guidance: An item may be stored before its glossary is ready, but it remains unavailable to members. Do not confuse stored with releasable.

selectionLimit.title: Member selection limit
selectionLimit.purpose: The catalog-wide limit decides how many Layer 2 intents one member may choose, up to the supported maximum of five.

actions.1: Select the reviewed limit and save against the current catalog revision.
actions.2: Confirm that member and profile copy still explains the number correctly.

selectionLimit.guidance: Lowering the limit does not remove existing excess choices. Affected members keep them until they next edit, so plan the transition.

catalog.title: Intent catalog
catalog.purpose: Every item has a permanent ID, one Layer 1 category, one reciprocal set, bilingual label, bilingual disclosure glossary, order and archive state.

actions.1: Open an item, update allowed copy or order and provide an audit reason.
actions.2: Review long-press glossary wording as carefully as the short label.

catalog.guidance: The glossary must plainly say who sees the answer. It is consent-facing product copy, not internal technical documentation.

reciprocalSets.title: Reciprocal disclosure sets
reciprocalSets.purpose: The set is the privacy boundary: a member's intent is revealed only to people who selected an item in that same set, never to an ordinary profile visitor.

actions.1: Check the set before an item first becomes live.
actions.2: Compare related items to ensure separate consent groups remain separate.

reciprocalSets.guidance: A live item's set is fixed. Moving it would merge audiences that consented separately, so create a replacement instead.

archiveRestore.title: Archive and restore
archiveRestore.purpose: Archive stops a Layer 2 item being offered to new selections while members who already chose it retain their stored choice.

actions.1: Archive an obsolete item with a clear audit reason.
actions.2: Restore only when the original meaning and disclosure set are still valid.

archiveRestore.guidance: Archive is reversible availability control, not deletion. Use a new item when meaning or disclosure audience changes.

conflicts.title: Revision conflicts and safe saves
conflicts.purpose: Item and catalog revisions prevent two administrators from silently overwriting one another's consent-sensitive changes.

actions.1: Review the server version when a conflict is returned.
actions.2: Reapply the intended edit deliberately and submit a fresh audited request.

conflicts.guidance: Never merge a stale Layer 2 draft automatically. The differences may change reciprocal disclosure or the global selection limit.

footprints.title: Footprints help
footprints.summary: A Footprint is a badge coin one member leaves on another member's profile, optionally with a short message. This page controls global limits, the badge catalog, who may send and receive each badge, member-specific allowances and reports of inappropriate Footprints.

steps.1: Review global allowance and message length before changing a badge or one member's exception.
steps.2: For a badge, check both sender and recipient audiences because both must permit the interaction.
steps.3: Handle open reports separately and confirm every resolved item or catalog mutation.

limits.title: Global daily and message limits
limits.purpose: The daily allowance caps how many Footprints a member may send, while message length bounds the optional text attached to a badge.

actions.1: Set reviewed bounded defaults for the whole product.
actions.2: Save the settings and confirm the refreshed values.

limits.guidance: A lower daily limit can affect all members immediately. It does not remove Footprints already sent or shorten existing messages.

badges.title: Badge catalog
badges.purpose: Each badge carries approved artwork, English and Hungarian meaning, order, active or archived state and two independent audience rules.

actions.1: Create or edit a badge with complete bilingual meaning and managed image.
actions.2: Set order and active state after previewing both audience summaries.

badges.guidance: The label explains the social meaning shown to members. Keep artwork and wording consistent so a recipient cannot reasonably misunderstand the signal.

twoSidedAudience.title: Sender and recipient audiences
twoSidedAudience.purpose: Sender rules govern the member viewing another profile and sending; recipient rules govern the profile owner who may receive that badge.

actions.1: Leave a side global when every eligible member should pass it.
actions.2: Select canonical genders or dynamic groups for a custom side and review the combined summary.

twoSidedAudience.guidance: Both sides must match, and within a custom side every configured dimension must match. An empty custom selection still means global, so use the explicit mode carefully.

memberOverride.title: Member-specific daily allowance
memberOverride.purpose: An override replaces the global daily send limit for one confirmed UID, including zero to prevent sending or blank to restore the default.

actions.1: Confirm the UID and enter the intended bounded allowance.
actions.2: Clear the value to return the member to the global default.

memberOverride.guidance: This is an operational exception, not a moderation ban. Use the member moderation panel when account restriction is the intended action.

reports.title: Reported Footprints
reports.purpose: Open and resolved tabs show who reported the interaction, who sent it, the badge, optional message, timing and resolution actor.

actions.1: Review the exact sender, recipient context, badge and message.
actions.2: Resolve an open report after completing any separate member moderation that policy requires.

reports.guidance: Resolve closes the report record; it does not automatically suspend the sender or rewrite the badge catalog. Use explicit moderation for broader consequences.

archiveBehavior.title: Archive a badge
archiveBehavior.purpose: Archiving removes a badge from future sends while preserving historical Footprints that already used it.

actions.1: Confirm the exact badge and its current audience before archive.
actions.2: Prefer temporary inactive state when a reviewed badge may return.

archiveBehavior.guidance: Archive is not deletion of member interaction history. Existing reports and sent badges retain the original stable identity.

pinger.title: Pinger help
pinger.summary: Pinger is Friending's lightweight interest signal: a member can indicate interest from another profile, and compatible states can feed the Collector or the guarded chat experience. This page owns its release policy, artwork and bilingual member copy.

steps.1: Keep the master and chat-contract gates off until the matching Core and client releases are proven.
steps.2: Review cooldown, retention and new-member defaults together with every member-facing message.
steps.3: Upload or select icon states, save one revision and confirm the audit record.

runtime.title: Runtime policy
runtime.purpose: The master switch, stable action identity, pair cooldown, Collector retention, chat contract version and default messaging gate define how Pinger behaves.

actions.1: Adjust bounded cooldown or retention only with the current product procedure.
actions.2: Enable the chat contract only after its migration readiness is explicitly reported.
actions.3: Choose whether new members default to receiving messages only from people they liked.

runtime.guidance: The stable action key is wire identity and must not change with wording. Rollout switches are safety gates, not data migration tools.

icons.title: Like and already-liked icons
icons.purpose: Four managed appearances cover the two interaction states in Light and Dark mode, or the app can use its bundled icon set.

actions.1: Upload a trusted PNG or SVG for each custom state and appearance.
actions.2: Select bundled icons for a complete built-in fallback without deleting staged custom artwork.

icons.guidance: Check that Like and Already liked remain visually distinct and readable in both appearances. Upload alone does not publish until configuration is saved.

copy.title: Bilingual member copy
copy.purpose: The catalog controls button accessibility, confirmations, Collector labels, chat prompts, push notifications and other Pinger messages in English and Hungarian.

actions.1: Edit both locales for every message key.
actions.2: Preserve each documented placeholder exactly and review the full interaction flow, not isolated sentences.

copy.guidance: Missing, duplicated or renamed placeholders make otherwise good copy invalid. Avoid promising delivery or access that the current runtime gates do not provide.

audit.title: Pinger audit trail
audit.purpose: Recent records identify configuration and icon operations, their actor, revision and time.

actions.1: Confirm that the expected save or upload operation was recorded.
actions.2: Use the full Audit log when a longer chronology is needed.

audit.guidance: An icon upload and a configuration save are separate operations. Confirm the publishing save rather than assuming an uploaded file became active.

inviteConfiguration.title: Mobile invitations help
inviteConfiguration.summary: Mobile invitations let a member invite someone by SMS. Webadmin decides whether Friending's server or the member's iPhone sends the message, which localized template is rendered, and whether an App Store storefront country overrides the global fallback.

steps.1: Review the global fallback because it applies when StoreKit supplies no usable storefront or no override matches.
steps.2: Choose the delivery mode with privacy and provider readiness in mind, then validate every required language template.
steps.3: Add only deliberate storefront overrides and review the complete dirty draft before saving.

globalFallback.title: Global fallback
globalFallback.purpose: The global rule controls whether invitations are available by default and which delivery mode and templates apply when no country override matches.

actions.1: Enable or disable mobile invitations globally.
actions.2: Select the fallback delivery mode and maintain its language templates.

globalFallback.guidance: Disabling the fallback hides mobile invitations everywhere unless product behavior explicitly supports an active override. Verify the resolved configuration before release.

deliveryModes.title: Server SMS or device composer
deliveryModes.purpose: Server SMS submits the selected phone number to Core for provider delivery; device SMS opens the iOS Messages composer and does not submit the recipient to the send endpoint.

actions.1: Choose server delivery only when provider credentials, rate limits and monitoring are ready.
actions.2: Choose device delivery when the member should review and send through their own carrier.

deliveryModes.guidance: The two modes have different privacy, cost and delivery semantics. Copy must not imply that Friending sent a device-composed message.

templates.title: Localized SMS templates
templates.purpose: Core renders the same administrator-owned message for both delivery modes, with English and Hungarian required and optional additional language codes.

actions.1: Write complete templates and retain the required profile-link token.
actions.2: Add a valid language code only when the matching client locale is supported.

templates.guidance: SMS length can change carrier segmentation and cost. Test the resolved link and accented Hungarian text rather than reviewing editor text alone.

storefrontOverrides.title: App Store storefront overrides
storefrontOverrides.purpose: An override applies a different active state, mode or template set for one StoreKit storefront country code.

actions.1: Add a canonical three-letter storefront code and configure only the intended difference.
actions.2: Remove an override to return that storefront to the global fallback.

storefrontOverrides.guidance: Storefront is read when the app opens this screen and is not written to the member profile. It may differ from residence or current location.

support.title: Support inbox help
support.summary: The Support inbox contains one direct operations conversation per member. Replies can reach the member through the in-app bell, realtime delivery and background push, while recent client context helps diagnose app-specific problems.

steps.1: Select the correct member thread by name and UID and read the full recent conversation before replying.
steps.2: Open Client details only for diagnostic context and inspect images only when the support case requires it.
steps.3: Send one clear response or normalized image and wait for a definitive result before retrying.

threadList.title: Member thread list
threadList.purpose: Rows show member identity, latest message, source platform, time and the operator-side unread count for each support conversation.

actions.1: Choose a thread by confirmed UID, not display name alone.
actions.2: Use unread badges and latest activity to prioritize pending support.

threadList.guidance: Opening a conversation clears the operator-side unread counter. Read the thread before switching away so work is not mistaken for completed support.

conversation.title: Conversation history
conversation.purpose: The message timeline separates member and administrator messages, text and image events, platform labels and delivery chronology.

actions.1: Read prior answers and member-provided context before composing a reply.
actions.2: Open a retained image in the protected lightbox when its content is relevant.

conversation.guidance: A removed image remains as a terminal event and must not be treated as a loading error. Avoid repeating advice already given in the thread.

clientContext.title: Client details
clientContext.purpose: The latest bounded context can show source platform, app or build information, device and accessibility settings useful for reproducing a problem.

actions.1: Expand diagnostics when the issue depends on Android, iOS or Web behavior.
actions.2: Use facts such as build and appearance settings to route or reproduce the report.

clientContext.guidance: Client context is diagnostic, may be absent or stale, and is not proof of member identity. Do not expose internal device detail unnecessarily in the reply.

attachments.title: Support images
attachments.purpose: Authorized image messages are served through a trusted media boundary, and outbound files are normalized to bounded, metadata-free JPEG before Core receives them.

actions.1: Open an inbound image only for the active support task.
actions.2: Attach a supported JPEG, PNG or WebP when a visual answer is genuinely useful, and reuse the offered retry after a known failed response.

attachments.guidance: Images may contain private member information. Do not download, reuse or forward them outside the conversation, and do not send credentials or private evidence.

reply.title: Compose and send
reply.purpose: The composer sends bounded text or one image to the selected UID and triggers the supported member notification channels.

actions.1: Write a direct, non-technical response with a clear next step.
actions.2: Send once, or use the exact preserved image retry when the UI offers it.

reply.guidance: A timeout can leave delivery uncertain. Re-read the conversation before creating a second logical message, especially when the first response may have landed.

helpCms.title: Help centre CMS guide
helpCms.summary: This CMS publishes the member-facing Friending Help centre. Categories organize discovery, while each article stores English and Hungarian title, summary, search keywords and a structured block body that publishes as one bilingual unit.

steps.1: Choose or create the category first, then open one article draft by its permanent slug.
steps.2: Complete and proofread both locale tabs, including structure, links, emphasis and warnings.
steps.3: Save a private draft for review or publish only when both languages are complete; archive obsolete articles instead of reusing their identity.

articleEditor.title: Article editor
articleEditor.purpose: The editor brings permanent identity, category, discovery settings, locale content and block structure into one versioned draft.

actions.1: Create a new article or open an existing draft, published or archived article.
actions.2: Save without publishing, or publish after the whole bilingual document passes validation.

articleEditor.guidance: Save draft is private; Publish is member-visible. A published correction goes live as one article, so review the complete result rather than only the changed sentence.

metadata.title: Slug, category and featured rank
metadata.purpose: The slug is permanent article identity, the category controls Help-home grouping, and featured rank can promote selected articles.

actions.1: Choose a clear lowercase slug when creating the article.
actions.2: Assign the correct category and use a positive featured rank only for intentional Help-home promotion.

metadata.guidance: Lower positive ranks appear first; zero means not featured. Never repurpose an existing slug for unrelated guidance because links and search history may depend on it.

languages.title: English and Hungarian content
languages.purpose: Each locale has its own member-facing title, summary, search keywords and body blocks while sharing one article lifecycle.

actions.1: Switch between EN and HU and provide equivalent, natural guidance in each.
actions.2: Add concise keywords that help member search without appearing in the article.

languages.guidance: Publishing requires both languages. Translate the intended action and product meaning, not just individual words or internal technical names.

contentBlocks.title: Structured content blocks
contentBlocks.purpose: Paragraphs, headings, lists, callouts and other bounded blocks build a readable article without accepting arbitrary HTML.

actions.1: Add the appropriate block type, edit its runs or list items and reorder it with the arrow controls.
actions.2: Apply supported emphasis, links and warning tones only where they improve comprehension.

contentBlocks.guidance: Keep steps task-oriented for members unfamiliar with Friending. Do not place secrets, private evidence links or unsupported markup in article content.

categories.title: Help categories
categories.purpose: Categories provide bilingual Help-home titles and summaries, stable key, display order, icon identity and active state.

actions.1: Create or edit category presentation in both languages.
actions.2: Reorder or deactivate a category when its collection should stop appearing to members.

categories.guidance: An inactive category disappears from the Help home. Review the articles assigned to it so useful published guidance does not become unexpectedly hard to find.

articleList.title: Article inventory
articleList.purpose: The table shows permanent slug, category, both localized titles, draft or published state and featured rank.

actions.1: Open the exact article for editing and compare both locale titles.
actions.2: Use status and rank to audit what members can currently discover.

articleList.guidance: A draft is never member-visible, and an archived article may retain complete content. Status must be read separately from content completeness.

publishing.title: Publish and archive lifecycle
publishing.purpose: Publish validates both locales and makes the article available; archive removes it from member surfaces while preserving the draft for future revision.

actions.1: Publish only after editorial and product review.
actions.2: Archive obsolete guidance and later republish the same stable article when its original topic returns.

publishing.guidance: Help content can change member behavior immediately. Verify links, instructions and current app terminology on the supported clients before publishing.

configuration.title: Configuration help
configuration.summary: Configuration contains only approved product controls that can change without a deployment. It covers reversible feature behavior, Join session timing, iOS appearance, global push delivery, public link origins, presence availability and the complete profile-video-verification member flow.

steps.1: Identify the exact product surface and read its current value, bounds and member consequence.
steps.2: Change one coherent setting group, including both languages where copy is involved.
steps.3: Save, refresh and verify the affected client or operational surface without using an unrelated production mutation as a test.

productControls.title: Allow-listed product controls
productControls.purpose: General settings include reversible switches such as People hero delivery and the isolated demo system, with type and bounds supplied by Core.

actions.1: Review the explanation and current server value for each exposed key.
actions.2: Change only a setting whose product impact and rollback are understood.

productControls.guidance: Turning a feature off normally preserves its records. Demo controls never merge demo and regular users, and a disabled hero response does not delete campaigns.

session.title: Join idle session timeout
session.purpose: The idle timeout decides how long a signed-in Join browser stays authenticated after the member's last real interaction.

actions.1: Set a whole number of minutes within the displayed bounds.
actions.2: Balance account security with realistic signup and profile-editing sessions.

session.guidance: Background realtime and polling do not count as activity. A shorter timeout can interrupt members who pause during onboarding or profile work.

appearance.title: iOS appearance mode
appearance.purpose: System follows the device's Light or Dark setting live, while Force Light and Force Dark override it for the whole iOS app.

actions.1: Keep System for member-controlled appearance in normal operation.
actions.2: Use a forced mode only for an explicitly tested product or emergency reason.

appearance.guidance: This affects every iOS screen from launch. Test contrast, media and modals throughout the app before forcing an appearance.

pushDelivery.title: Global push delivery mode
pushDelivery.purpose: The mode enables FCM, OneSignal or both provider channels for Core's provider-agnostic push worker; Both handles eligible channels independently.

actions.1: Confirm current member-registration coverage and provider readiness before narrowing the mode.
actions.2: Save one deliberate mode change, wait for the canonical Core response and verify the operational effect without sending a routine test push.

pushDelivery.guidance: This setting does not register devices, configure provider credentials or prove delivery. After an uncertain response, the page reloads authoritative settings before allowing another gesture.

publicLinks.title: Website and profile-link origins
publicLinks.purpose: The website origin builds browser legal and marketing links; the profile origin mints shareable profile links and QR codes recognized by released apps.

actions.1: Choose only HTTPS origins offered or accepted by the corresponding policy.
actions.2: Verify generated legal links, profile links, QR behavior and browser fallback.

publicLinks.guidance: A profile host also needs support in signed app associated domains for direct app opening. An unknown profile origin can remove the in-app QR experience.

presence.title: Profile presence modes
presence.purpose: Presence configuration decides which availability choices members can use and how bilingual labels explain those modes.

actions.1: Review mandatory and optional modes, counts and current revision.
actions.2: Update localized presentation or availability and confirm any affected-member reconciliation.

presence.guidance: Disabling a mode can rewrite affected member profiles to a safe fallback. Treat it as a data-impacting change, not copy-only configuration.

verificationFlow.title: Profile video verification flow
verificationFlow.purpose: This editor owns status cards, introduction, camera guidance, preview, detailed owner messages, challenge prompts, consent and privacy link in both languages and appearances.

actions.1: Review every step as one member journey and keep both required head turns plus an enabled expression.
actions.2: Maintain accurate consent, purpose, retention, withdrawal and deletion copy before enabling the flow.
actions.3: Preview Light and Dark colors and save against the independent verification revision.

verificationFlow.guidance: The flow proves a manual video-to-current-photo comparison only. It must not claim identity-document verification, automated liveness or general member safety.

safetyBoundary.title: Safe configuration boundary
safetyBoundary.purpose: The final notice explains why infrastructure hosts, databases, signing keys, provider credentials and other secrets are intentionally absent from browser editing.

actions.1: Use this page only for the named product controls.
actions.2: Follow the deployment or secret-management procedure for anything outside the allow-list.

safetyBoundary.guidance: A missing infrastructure control is a security property, not an incomplete screen. Never move a secret into Webadmin to make it editable.

appReview.title: App Review sandbox help
appReview.summary: The sandbox is a deterministic, synthetic account used by platform reviewers to experience a populated Friending app. Core owns its fixed identity, fixture, full deletion and same-UID reprovisioning; Webadmin shows readiness and offers one tightly scoped reset.

steps.1: Confirm the control record, lifecycle and fixture version before interpreting any count or check.
steps.2: Read all count witnesses and readiness checks; one failed check means the sandbox is not ready.
steps.3: Reset only when repair is required, using the exact phrase and durable pending request already retained by the page.

identity.title: Reviewer identity
identity.purpose: When authorized by Core, this area identifies the fixed synthetic reviewer account and shows whether review login is configured without exposing its access code.

actions.1: Confirm the expected fixed UID and synthetic markers when they are projected to your role.
actions.2: Check configuration presence without requesting or revealing the plaintext review code.

identity.guidance: Hidden identity fields are an intentional role boundary. The review code never belongs in browser JavaScript, screenshots, tickets or Git.

control.title: Fixture control and lifecycle
control.purpose: The control record names fixture version, revision, reset state, account lifecycle, media manifest and last converged receipt.

actions.1: Verify that the control is ready, no reset is in progress and lifecycle agrees with the account state.
actions.2: Use revision and receipt information to understand the latest reset or automatic restore.

control.guidance: A reviewer-initiated deletion must use the normal full erasure path. Scheduled recovery then provisions a clean account; Webadmin must not weaken deletion to preserve the fixture.

counts.title: Scoped document witnesses
counts.purpose: The complete count census covers profile, media, relationships, chats, notifications, membership and Dates records belonging to the protected fixture scope.

actions.1: Compare every actual count with its expected witness.
actions.2: Use a mismatch to identify which fixture area needs a guarded reset or server investigation.

counts.guidance: Counts alone do not prove meaningful content or valid media. They must be read together with all semantic checks.

checks.title: Readiness checks
checks.purpose: The 33 closed checks prove control, environment match, account state, complete content, valid media, PLUS access and Dates semantics.

actions.1: Inspect every failing check and its associated count or lifecycle clue.
actions.2: Claim readiness only when the complete set is green.

checks.guidance: A partial green page is not release-ready. The parser intentionally rejects unknown or incomplete successful payloads rather than hiding missing checks.

reset.title: Guarded reset to baseline
reset.purpose: Reset transactionally reconciles only the protected fixture and reviewer-keyed runtime rows, then validates post-commit media and product semantics.

actions.1: Read current state and type the exact confirmation phrase.
actions.2: Submit once and let the page reuse its persisted request ID and expected revision after timeout or reload.
actions.3: Wait for exact convergence before clearing or starting another reset.

reset.guidance: Never invent a new request after an uncertain response. The durable pair prevents duplicate logical resets and unrelated live members must never be touched.

interpretation.title: What readiness does and does not prove
interpretation.purpose: A green fixture proves the server-side synthetic experience is complete and resettable; it does not prove App Store credentials, signed app behavior or the final physical-device walkthrough.

actions.1: Use the page as fixture evidence for release preparation.
actions.2: Track signed-device review login and walkthrough as separate external gates.

interpretation.guidance: Do not turn a green Webadmin status into a claim that provider, purchase or physical-device gates are complete.

admins.title: Admin users help
admins.summary: This owner-controlled allow-list decides which email addresses may request a short-lived Webadmin sign-in code. Active membership is rechecked by Core on every dashboard render and every admin proxy call.

steps.1: Confirm the person's approved operational role and exact email through the owner process.
steps.2: Add or reactivate only that address and verify the role and active state returned by Core.
steps.3: Disable or remove access immediately when authority ends, then confirm the audit event.

addAdmin.title: Add an administrator address
addAdmin.purpose: The form adds one validated email to the Core-owned administrator allow-list under the established default role policy.

actions.1: Enter the exact approved email address.
actions.2: Submit once and verify that the new row appears with the intended state.

addAdmin.guidance: Adding an address grants access to request a login code; it does not send or reveal a permanent password. Confirm authorization outside Webadmin first.

roles.title: Administrator roles
roles.purpose: Rows show owner, admin or viewer role so operators understand whether an account may manage access, perform edits or only read.

actions.1: Review role beside email and activity before changing access state.
actions.2: Use the approved owner process for any role change not offered by this screen.

roles.guidance: The UI does not reconstruct permissions from labels. Core remains authoritative, and Dates or catalog capabilities can add separate bounded ladders.

activeAccess.title: Active state, lock and removal
activeAccess.purpose: Owners can enable or disable membership, clear an active login-code lock, or remove another administrator record.

actions.1: Disable for an immediate reversible access stop.
actions.2: Clear a temporary lock only after understanding why it was triggered.
actions.3: Remove an obsolete administrator after confirming the exact email.

activeAccess.guidance: Revocation is rechecked on every protected request, so an existing browser cookie does not preserve access. Removing a row is stronger than clearing a temporary login lock.

ownerBoundary.title: Owner-only safety boundary
ownerBoundary.purpose: Administrator allow-list mutations are owner-only and self-protection prevents an owner from accidentally disabling or deleting the account currently in use.

actions.1: Use a different approved owner for changes to your own active account.
actions.2: Confirm at least one valid owner path remains before removing another administrator.

ownerBoundary.guidance: A missing or disabled control is intentional protection. Do not bypass it through a lower-level Core call.

audit.title: Audit log help
audit.summary: The Audit log is the chronological, server-authored record of administrative mutations and sensitive operations. It identifies who acted, what operation ran, which target was involved and a deliberately safe subset of details.

steps.1: Refresh before investigating a recent change and start from the newest page.
steps.2: Match actor, action, target and timestamp to the operational event in question.
steps.3: Read safe details and withheld counts without expecting raw payloads or secrets.

navigation.title: Refresh and pagination
navigation.purpose: The page loads a bounded newest-first timeline and lets operators refresh or move through older server pages.

actions.1: Refresh after an expected operation to request the authoritative latest rows.
actions.2: Use Previous and Next to inspect older chronology without altering audit data.

navigation.guidance: The audit log is immutable from this screen and intentionally has no arbitrary browser-side query or delete control.

eventRows.title: Actor, action, target and time
eventRows.purpose: Each row anchors an administrative event to the authenticated email, stable action name, bounded target and server timestamp.

actions.1: Use the four fields together to distinguish similar repeated operations.
actions.2: Compare the event with the affected page's refreshed state or dedicated history.

eventRows.guidance: An audit row proves that Core recorded the operation, not that an external provider or client completed every downstream effect.

safeDetails.title: Safe detail projection
safeDetails.purpose: Only explicitly allow-listed scalar fields are rendered; nested, unknown, empty or overlong material is withheld and counted rather than exposed.

actions.1: Read the visible key-value pairs as bounded context.
actions.2: Note the withheld count when escalating through an authorized server-side investigation.

safeDetails.guidance: Withheld does not mean missing evidence. It protects secrets, private data and unbounded payloads from entering the browser or screenshots.

runtimeHelp.title: Runtime settings help
runtimeHelp.intro: This guide describes the Core-owned behavior behind every Dates runtime setting. It shows the value currently returned by Core, the stored value, the safe default and the validation bounds. Saving a value is immediate for new requests, but it does not migrate existing records or start background infrastructure.
runtimeHelp.beforeChangingCopy: Treat feature switches, retention rules and workers as one release unit. Use this order when enabling Dates or a high-impact capability:
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepRetention: Approve the privacy and legal retention values, especially live trails and moderation evidence.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepWorker: Deploy and verify the Dates background worker, monitoring and delivery dependencies.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepMaster: Enable the master Dates switch for a controlled audience and verify bootstrap, list and detail reads.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepCapabilities: Enable creation, live sharing, reviews and digest separately; do not switch them all on at once.
runtimeHelp.rolloutStepVerify: Watch errors, moderation queues, worker lag and audit logs before widening rollout.
runtimeHelp.effectiveNote: When the master switch is OFF, Core forces every subordinate feature switch to an effective OFF even if its stored value is ON. The effective value is what the app actually receives.
runtimeHelp.timingNote: Durations and retention values are usually copied into a record when an activity, decline, case or purge schedule is created. Changing the default does not rewrite existing deadlines unless a dedicated migration or operation does so.
runtimeHelp.unknownCopy: Core returned settings that are not part of this Webadmin release's bounded help catalog.
runtimeHelp.unknownSettingCopy: Do not change this setting until the matching Core release notes and operating procedure have been reviewed.
